description: Use for 'how are crypto gains and company profits taxed in X' — e.g. 'tax on selling bitcoin in Portugal', 'corporate tax rate in Paraguay', 'special tax regimes Italy'. Give the country (ISO-3166 code or English name), optional `tax_type` filter (`income` | `corporate` | `vat` | `capital_gains` | `crypto`). Returns, per rate, the source's own wording in `as_reported`, its first percentage as `rate`, a `conditional` flag (true when the wording is a range or has conditions — quote `as_reported` then) and an `applies_to` label; plus special regimes, crypto tier, last_verified and sources. `territorial_vs_worldwide` is set only for the few countries the dataset flags as territorial; null means not flagged, not 'worldwide'. Scope: `corporate` is the headline company rate; the other figures describe how CRYPTO is taxed. General salary/employment income tax brackets and the consumer VAT rate are NOT in this dataset — tell the person that rather than quoting these numbers as such. Separately, `general_rates` gives the OECD's general statutory rates where the OECD covers the country: `corporate_income_tax` (the combined company rate: central plus a representative sub-national rate and surcharges, so it can differ from the crypto source's `corporate`) and `top_personal_income_tax`, each with `rate`, `year`, `measure` and the OECD citation in `source`; null means not covered by the OECD table, or held back because the source value looks wrong (then listed under `general_rates.withheld` with the reason), never zero; `vat` is always null. These are national figures and do not describe a particular state or region. `found: false` means no crypto-tax rows for the country; `general_rates` can still be filled. For side-by-side country comparisons use tax_compare.

country.description: Country to look up: ISO-3166 alpha-2/alpha-3 code or English name, e.g. 'PT', 'PRT', 'Portugal'.

tax_type.description: Return only this rate. Omit to get all five.

name: get_tax_rates
title: Get crypto and company tax rates
